title: Factorization Machines
summary: Rendle's original FM: models all pairwise feature interactions via factorized (embedding-dot-product) parameters instead of dense weights per cross, computable in linear time, and robust under the extreme sparsity typical of one-hot categorical recommender data.
expected_effect: Models every pairwise feature interaction through shared low-rank embeddings, so interactions can be estimated even for pairs that are rare or unseen in training. A strong default for sparse, high-cardinality categorical data; limited to second-order interactions by construction.

title: DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
summary: Shares a single embedding layer between an FM component (2nd-order interactions) and a DNN component (implicit higher-order interactions), trained end-to-end with no manual feature engineering.
expected_effect: Adds an MLP over concatenated embeddings alongside the FM term, to capture higher-order interactions the bilinear form cannot express. The deep tower needs enough data per feature to fit; on small or sparse feature sets it mostly adds variance.

title: xDeepFM: Combining Explicit and Implicit Feature Interactions for Recommender Systems
summary: Adds a Compressed Interaction Network (CIN) that produces explicit, vector-wise, bounded-degree feature crosses on top of the implicit DNN interactions used by DeepFM.
expected_effect: Adds a Compressed Interaction Network that produces explicit, bounded-degree interactions at the vector level alongside an MLP. More expressive than FM, with correspondingly more parameters to fit.

title: Deep & Cross Network for Ad Click Predictions
summary: Adds a cross network that applies explicit feature crossing at each layer with a bounded polynomial degree, run alongside a standard DNN, adding negligible extra parameters.
expected_effect: Stacks explicit polynomial cross layers with a deep tower, giving bounded-degree feature crosses with far fewer parameters than an equivalent MLP.

title: DCN V2: Improved Deep & Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems
summary: Replaces DCN's cross vector with a more expressive low-rank matrix formulation (optionally a mixture of low-rank experts), addressing DCN v1's limited expressiveness at scale.
expected_effect: Replaces DCN's vector cross with a low-rank matrix cross, raising capacity per cross layer; designed for large-scale industrial CTR workloads.

title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks
summary: Maps features into a shared low-dimensional space and stacks multi-head self-attention layers with residual connections so each layer models increasingly higher-order feature combinations.
expected_effect: Uses multi-head self-attention over feature embeddings to learn which interactions matter rather than enumerating them, giving interpretable attention weights over feature pairs.

title: FiBiNET: Combining Feature Importance and Bilinear feature Interaction for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Uses a Squeeze-and-Excitation network to dynamically re-weight feature embeddings by importance, then applies bilinear functions instead of inner/Hadamard product for interaction.
expected_effect: Uses a SENET block to reweight feature importance dynamically and bilinear functions for finer-grained interaction modelling than an inner or Hadamard product.

title: Product-based Neural Networks for User Response Prediction
summary: Inserts a product layer between the embedding layer and the fully-connected layers to explicitly capture pairwise interactive patterns across feature fields before the DNN.
expected_effect: Inserts an explicit product layer between the embedding layer and the MLP so multiplicative interactions are directly available to the deep tower instead of being learned implicitly.

title: Neural Factorization Machines for Sparse Predictive Analytics
summary: Introduces a Bilinear Interaction pooling layer that lets a single shallow hidden layer model second-order feature interactions, combining FM linearity with neural non-linearity.
expected_effect: Replaces FM's summed second-order term with a bi-interaction pooling layer feeding an MLP, so nonlinearity is applied on top of interactions rather than beside them.

title: Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems
summary: Jointly trains a wide linear model over cross-product features with a deep neural network over embeddings, so the wide part memorizes frequent co-occurrences while the deep part generalizes to unseen combinations.
expected_effect: Jointly trains a wide linear model over cross-product features (memorisation) with a deep tower (generalisation), on the argument that neither alone covers both regimes.

title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Uses a local activation unit to adaptively attend over a user's historical behavior sequence with respect to a candidate item, instead of squashing history into one fixed vector.
expected_effect: A strong, promising direction: KuaiRand-Pure's interaction logs let you build each user's watched-video history, and DIN-style target-attention over that history (attending to past videos by similarity to the candidate video's author/tag/category) should beat feature-cross-only models like DeepFM. Only use PAST interactions as history inputs -- never include the current row's post-click columns when building the sequence for that row.

title: Deep Interest Evolution Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: Extends DIN with an interest extractor GRU layer and an attention-based interest evolving layer to model how user interest drifts over time relative to the target item.
expected_effect: Higher potential ceiling than DIN by modeling interest drift, but heavier to implement and tune (auxiliary loss for the GRU, two-stage attention) -- reasonable only after a plain DIN has been tried and shown behavior-sequence modeling helps on this dataset.

title: Behavior Sequence Transformer for E-commerce Recommendation in Alibaba
summary: Applies a Transformer self-attention encoder over the user's behavior sequence to capture sequential signal, instead of just concatenating behavior features as prior CTR models did.
expected_effect: Good middle ground between DIN and full sequential recommenders (SASRec): self-attention over each user's clicked-video history, then fused with the FM/DeepFM-style feature-cross tower for the final click score. On 27K users / 7.6K videos, sequences are short enough that a small Transformer trains fast.

title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
summary: A two-layer self-attention (Transformer-style) sequence model that predicts the next item from a user's action history, capturing long-range dependencies like an RNN but attending directly to the relevant few past actions.
expected_effect: Framed originally for next-item prediction rather than per-row click scoring; on KuaiRand-Pure it is best used as a user-history encoder feeding a click-scoring head rather than swapped in wholesale, since the task here is ranking candidate videos for is_click, not autoregressive next-item generation. Consider it after BST if sequence order (not just recency) matters.

title: Session-based Recommendations with Recurrent Neural Networks
summary: Models user sessions with a GRU-based RNN to predict the probability of the next event (e.g. item click) given the session so far; an early and still-common strong RNN baseline for sequential recommendation.
expected_effect: Cheaper than a Transformer-based sequence encoder and a reasonable lightweight alternative to BST/SASRec for encoding per-user watch history on KuaiRand-Pure, but generally weaker than attention-based sequence models at this data scale -- try it mainly as a fast baseline for whether sequence modeling helps at all before investing in BST/DIEN.

title: Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts
summary: Replaces a shared-bottom multi-task network with multiple expert subnetworks and a per-task gating network, letting each task learn its own weighting over shared experts.
expected_effect: KuaiRand-Pure exposes 12 feedback signals (is_like, is_follow, is_comment, is_forward, long_view, play_time_ms, ...) but only is_click is scored. MMoE lets is_click share expert capacity with these auxiliary signals as extra training heads, which can regularize embeddings on this comparatively small (1.4M-row) dataset. Only the is_click head's output is used for GAUC/nDCG scoring; the auxiliary heads must never feed back post-click columns as *inputs* for predicting is_click on the same row (label leakage) -- they are outputs only.

title: Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning (MTL) Model for Personalized Recommendations
summary: Separates task-shared experts from task-specific experts and stacks them with progressive routing layers, explicitly addressing negative transfer and the seesaw effect that MMoE still shows.
expected_effect: A step up from MMoE for the same KuaiRand-Pure auxiliary-signal setup (click plus like/follow/comment/forward/long_view/etc.) if MMoE shows negative transfer (auxiliary tasks hurting the click head). More parameters and tuning surface than MMoE, so only justified once MMoE's seesaw effect is actually observed.

title: Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate
summary: Trains a post-click target jointly with the click target via the chain-rule identity P(click, post-click) = P(click) x P(post-click | click), estimated over the entire impression space, removing the sample-selection bias of training the post-click model on clicked-only rows.
expected_effect: Not directly about CVR here, but the underlying structure maps cleanly onto KuaiRand-Pure: several of the 12 feedback signals (long_view, is_like, is_comment, play_time_ms-derived signals) are only meaningful *after* a click, exactly like ESMM's conversion. Model P(click) x P(signal | click) over the whole impression space instead of training a signal-specific auxiliary head only on clicked rows, then use it only to shape shared embeddings -- the scored metric is still GAUC/nDCG on the click head alone.

title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
summary: Derives a generic pairwise ranking criterion (BPR-Opt) from a Bayesian analysis of implicit feedback, optimizing that for a given user, observed (clicked) items should be ranked above unobserved ones, rather than optimizing pointwise classification accuracy.
expected_effect: Optimises a pairwise ranking objective over (user, positive, negative) triples. Designed for sparse implicit feedback where only positives are observed and unobserved items are treated as weak negatives; it optimises ordering rather than calibrated probability.

title: From RankNet to LambdaRank to LambdaMART: An Overview
summary: Overview of RankNet, LambdaRank, and LambdaMART -- LambdaRank optimizes a smoothed surrogate for ranking metrics like NDCG directly via gradients ('lambdas') weighted by the metric change from swapping a pair, and LambdaMART is its gradient-boosted-tree version.
expected_effect: Optimises a smoothed surrogate for a ranking metric directly, weighting each pairwise gradient by the metric change that swapping the pair would cause. Requires query grouping (here, per-user grouping) and targets rank order rather than calibrated probabilities.

title: Sampling-Bias-Corrected Neural Modeling for Large Corpus Item Recommendations
summary: Trains a two-tower retrieval model with in-batch negatives, and shows plain in-batch sampling is biased toward popular items unless corrected by an estimated item-sampling-probability term subtracted from the logits.
expected_effect: Relevant mainly if the pipeline frames click prediction as scoring (user, video) pairs against in-batch negatives instead of pure pointwise BCE -- with only 7.6K videos, popularity skew is real and the sampling-bias correction is cheap to add; without it, in-batch negative training will over-penalize popular videos. Lower priority than BPR/LambdaMART for this task's per-row pointwise setup, but worth it if moving toward a two-tower or listwise formulation.

title: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
summary: A histogram-based, leaf-wise gradient boosted decision tree framework with gradient-based one-side sampling and exclusive feature bundling for speed and memory efficiency at large scale.
expected_effect: Very strong, very cheap baseline-beater for KuaiRand-Pure: 1.4M rows with mostly categorical/count features is exactly GBDT's sweet spot, it needs no embedding tuning, trains in well under a minute on CPU, and LightGBM's built-in `lambdarank` objective (grouped by user) directly targets NDCG -- likely one of the best score-per-compute options in this whole KB for this dataset.

title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
summary: A scalable, regularized gradient tree boosting system with a sparsity-aware split algorithm and weighted quantile sketch for approximate learning, widely used for tabular prediction tasks.
expected_effect: Comparable to LightGBM as a cheap baseline-beater on this dataset's tabular categorical/count features; XGBoost's `rank:ndcg` / `rank:pairwise` objectives (grouped by user_id) give the same NDCG-targeting benefit as LightGBM's lambdarank -- pick either GBDT library, the choice matters less than actually grouping by user and using a ranking objective instead of plain binary logloss.

title: Doubly Robust Policy Evaluation and Learning
summary: For contextual-bandit-style logged data (context, action taken, reward observed, but not rewards for untaken actions), combines an inverse-propensity-weighted estimator with a reward model into a doubly-robust estimator with lower variance than either alone.
expected_effect: ADVANCED / OPTIONAL. KuaiRand-Pure's `log_random_*` files log interactions under fully random exposure, which is exactly the unbiased logging policy IPS/doubly-robust methods need as a comparison point -- they can be used to (a) sanity-check whether the main click model is biased toward popular/previously-shown videos, or (b) build a debiased evaluation signal alongside GAUC/nDCG. High effort for uncertain payoff relative to the primary metric; pursue only after the modeling directions above have been exhausted.

title: KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos
summary: Introduces the KuaiRand family of datasets (of which KuaiRand-Pure is the smallest variant): short-video interaction logs from Kuaishou with rich user/video side features and, critically, a subset of interactions collected under fully random video exposure rather than the production ranking policy, enabling unbiased offline evaluation and debiasing research.
expected_effect: The primary reference for what fields exist and mean on this task: user features (activity level, follower counts, register days, 18 onehot features) and video features (author_id, video_type, upload_type, music_id, tag, duration, statistics) are safe pre-click inputs; post-click columns (play_time_ms, long_view, profile_stay_time, and similar) must NEVER be used as inputs when predicting is_click on the same row -- that is direct label leakage, since they only exist because a click already happened. The `log_random_*` files are the source data for the counterfactual/IPS direction above.

title: Rank Aggregation Methods for the Web
summary: Formalizes combining several ranked lists into one, comparing footrule- and Kendall-tau-based optimal aggregation against simple positional voting methods such as Borda count, originally for meta-search.
expected_effect: Formalises combining several ranked lists into one. Positional methods such as Borda count are cheap and robust compared with optimal footrule/Kendall-tau aggregation. The classical result is that aggregating several diverse rankers can outperform any individual ranker, with the gain driven by how much the rankers disagree. Scores from different models are not on comparable scales, so aggregation is defined over ranks.

title: Bagging Predictors
summary: Trains multiple predictors on bootstrap resamples of the training set and averages (or votes over) their predictions, reducing variance for unstable base learners.
expected_effect: Trains predictors on bootstrap resamples and averages them, reducing variance for unstable base learners. The gain comes from decorrelating errors, so averaging near-identical models buys very little.

title: Stacked Generalization
summary: Trains a meta-learner on the out-of-fold predictions of several base learners to combine them, correcting each base learner's bias instead of averaging naively.
expected_effect: Trains a meta-learner on the out-of-fold predictions of several base learners, correcting each learner's bias instead of averaging naively. Needs enough held-out data to fit the combiner without overfitting it.

title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks
summary: Maps both categorical and NUMERIC fields into a shared low-dimensional space -- a scalar field is embedded as value * field_embedding -- so continuous quantities take part in the same learned interactions as ids, rather than being bucketised away first.
expected_effect: Reported by the authors as a way to let continuous fields participate in learned crosses without discretisation loss.

title: Practical Lessons from Predicting Clicks on Ads at Facebook
summary: Boosted trees consume raw continuous features directly and learn their own thresholds, then their leaf indices are fed to a linear model as categorical features. The paper's point is that trees are a supervised discretiser for numeric inputs.
expected_effect: Described as a way to combine numeric-native tree splits with a sparse linear/factorisation model.

title: On Embeddings for Numerical Features in Tabular Deep Learning
summary: Compares ways of feeding scalar features to deep models: raw, quantile-binned, piecewise-linear encodings and periodic (Fourier) activations. Reports that how a numeric feature is encoded changes results as much as the architecture around it.
expected_effect: Presented as evidence that the encoding of a scalar input is itself a design decision, not a preprocessing detail.

title: Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations
summary: Continuous inputs are normalised to a quantile-uniform scale and additionally supplied as powers and roots of that value, letting the network form sub- and super-linear responses. Also feeds age-of-item explicitly so the model can represent freshness rather than average it away.
expected_effect: Authors report heavy-tailed raw counts being unusable until transformed, and explicit recency inputs changing behaviour on fresh items.

title: Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems
summary: Combines a wide memorising component over sparse crosses with a deep generalising component over dense/continuous inputs, on the argument that the two capture different structure and neither subsumes the other.
expected_effect: Framed by the authors as complementary rather than competing components.
